quote.text: The Stone Age did not end for lack of stone, and the Oil Age will end long before the world runs out of oil.
quote.author: Sheikh Ahmed Zaki Yamani, Saudi oil minister 1962–1986

stories.kicker: Iran & the Gulf · The war reaches a second chokepoint
stories.headline: Yemen’s Houthis take a Red Sea port, and the war finds a new gate
stories.dek: A conflict fought all summer over the Strait of Hormuz opened a second front this week — the seizure of Mocha and a Houthi push toward Bab el-Mandeb — while a fresh exchange of fire kept the first strait a combat zone and drove Brent past a hundred and four dollars.

stories.headline: A raise the opposition backs, and a fight over what the public may see
stories.dek: The House spent Thursday on the political-salary rise announced a week earlier. The striking part was the agreement: the Workers’ Party endorsed the increase and pressed instead on disclosure — and no vote was ever taken.

stories.kicker: Down the Rabbit Hole · Tabletop miniature painting
stories.headline: The grown men thinning their paints
stories.dek: A hobby that sits between gaming and fine art, where a plastic soldier the size of a thumb becomes a canvas — and where a one-coat paint revolution has quietly pulled hundreds of thousands of newcomers over the skill wall.

stories.kicker: Buy It Once · Japanese selvedge denim
stories.headline: The self-finished edge, from the loom up
stories.dek: A pair of raw Japanese jeans is a maker’s object disguised as a wardrobe basic. Learn the mechanism — the shuttle loom, the rope-dyed indigo, the ounce weight — and you can judge any pair cold, and see where the price turns to theatre.

stories.kicker: Capital markets · The lab opens its books
stories.headline: DeepSeek files to list in Shanghai — and agrees to be seen
stories.dek: China’s most talked-about AI lab has picked a stock exchange, not a chip, as its next front. A listing would force the famously opaque firm to publish audited accounts — two weeks before Xi Jinping visits Washington’s rival.

stories.headline: The Apple Watch Ultra 4: a better computer in last year’s body
stories.dek: Apple’s toughest watch gains a faster chip, denser health sensing and a longer battery — in a case identical to the Ultra 3. The buyers polled wanted the battery. They did not ask for the intelligence.

stories.headline: Tudor revives a flop — and this time the movement earns it
stories.dek: The angular North Flag left the catalogue years ago, unloved. It returns from Geneva with a proper flyer GMT and a Master Chronometer stamp: substance the original lacked, wrapped in a case not everyone forgave.

stories.kicker: Film · Venice, on the eve of its verdict
stories.headline: Two ovations run ahead of their reviews — and the Lion waits a day
stories.dek: The eighty-third Venice Film Festival hands out its Golden Lion on Saturday, the day after this book prints. What is settled are the honours; what is loud are two premieres whose applause outpaced their notices.

stories.headline: The newest study points at sleep and exercise, not the phone itself
stories.dek: A 2026 analysis of more than fifty thousand children finds the harm from heavy screen use runs largely through what it displaces — rest and movement. For a twelve-year-old in an exam year, that is the useful news.

stories.kicker: The Big Picture · The oil shock nobody can ease into
stories.headline: Three central banks tighten into the same barrel
stories.dek: An oil-driven reflation has forced a synchronised hawkish turn: the ECB hiked, the Fed is priced to follow, and the ten-year yield hit its highest since 2007. The result is a bond bear and an equity wobble at once — diversification is not working.

stories.kicker: The Long Game · The supplement and the barbell
stories.headline: Creatine works after sixty — but only with the lifting
stories.dek: A 2026 meta-analysis pools the trials on creatine and resistance training in older adults. The gains are real in the legs and in lean mass; the catch is that none of them show up without the training itself.

stories.kicker: What’s Worth Booking · The dated agenda
stories.headline: What to book this week — and to plan the flights for
The country music of the rice fields learned to sell
stories.dek: Thailand’s growth story is told through Bangkok malls. But the real consumer frontier is its poorest, most populous region — and a century-old folk opera called mor lam has become the largest concert format in the country, and the arena where the nation’s brands now fight for it.
